# Quantum Backpropagation Frames

> Single-copy limits and constructive measurements for quantum-gradient readout,
> with full proofs, executable examples, and reproducible resource analysis.

Repository: https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Quantum-Backpropagation-Frames
Author: Ruge Lin. Original code and documentation: MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 Ruge Lin.
This index supports relevance assessment and source navigation. The linked
theory and evidence pages contain the formal statements and their support.

## When this repository is relevant

- How accurately can one shared measurement estimate every original coordinate
  of a quantum gradient from known tangent directions and an unknown response?
- What is the single-copy minimax trace variance of a universally unbiased POVM
  estimator with a supplied coherent reference and a real pure response?
- How can a sparse attaining POVM use reference interference, signed scores,
  and zero-score outcomes to reconstruct the complete classical gradient?
- What logical circuits and classical processing implement disjoint-block or
  overlapping-interval tangent readout, and how do variance and total work differ?

Related search terms: quantum-gradient readout; quantum backpropagation frames;
globally unbiased quantum estimation; equal-spectrum tangent matrix;
row-norm reference readout; sparse POVM; measurement and decoder resource costs.

## Core result and assumptions

A known real N-by-P matrix T satisfies T^T|0> = 0. The unknown q is any real unit
vector in dimension N. The target is the full original P-coordinate vector
g(q) = 2T^Tq. Each trial receives one copy of
Omega(q) = (|0>|0> + |1>|q>)/sqrt(2), including its coherent relative phase.
One fixed overall measurement and decoder may depend on T, but not q; they are
unbiased for every allowed q and have finite second moments. Ancillas and
randomized settings belong to the overall POVM; individual settings need not
be unbiased separately.

If T^T T has rank r >= 1 and all its nonzero eigenvalues equal lambda > 0,
the exact minimax trace risk is lambda * max{2r, 4(r-1)}. A measurement with
at most 2r+1 effects attains it. This is an upper bound on effect count, not a
minimum-outcome theorem. Zero-score outcomes count in the averaging denominator.

## Read, verify, and reuse

- [Worked tutorial](https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Quantum-Backpropagation-Frames/blob/main/docs/TUTORIAL.md): a complete two-qubit example, probabilities, scores, averaging, and self-checks.
- [Theorem and full proof](https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Quantum-Backpropagation-Frames/blob/main/docs/THEORY.md): exact quantifiers, both lower bounds, and the attaining POVM.
- [Constructive circuits](https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Quantum-Backpropagation-Frames/blob/main/docs/COMPILERS.md): disjoint and interval constructions, physical-bit processing, and charged costs.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Quantum-Backpropagation-Frames/blob/main/docs/IMPLEMENTATION.md): supported qbp_frames interfaces, parameter and bit order, full-angle rotations, and numerical limits.
- [Reproduction](https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Quantum-Backpropagation-Frames/blob/main/docs/REPRODUCIBILITY.md): installation, small executable example, larger compiler-only example, and bounded validation commands.
- [Evidence index](https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Quantum-Backpropagation-Frames/blob/main/docs/EVIDENCE.md): claims mapped to proofs, code, tests, retained data, and source hashes.
- [Comparisons and limitations](https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Quantum-Backpropagation-Frames/blob/main/docs/COMPARISONS.md): eligible baselines, access models, global versus local unbiasedness, and negative parity evidence.
- [Related work](https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Quantum-Backpropagation-Frames/blob/main/docs/RELATED_WORK.md): established ingredients and the relationship to prior research.
- [Citation metadata](https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Quantum-Backpropagation-Frames/blob/main/CITATION.cff): repository attribution; identify the commit used when citing a result or implementation.

## Applicability boundaries

The disjoint one-layer family has a linear-size logical realization attaining
risk 4P-8 at its zero-angle flat point, versus the no-mask benchmark 4P. The
constant gap is not an asymptotic runtime advantage. The overlapping-interval
row-norm compiler uses O(n * 2^w) logical gates for n system qubits and maximum
tangent interval width w, with variance at most 4 tr(T^T T). Its coordinate-row
support need not equal the tangent span; it is not a generic exact minimax
construction. Preparation, table construction, decoding, storage, precision,
and full-coordinate output remain costs.

The exact theorem is restricted to real pure responses and single-copy,
universally unbiased estimation. Complex or mixed responses, biased or
collective estimation, and extra coherent access are different models.
The restricted phase/Walsh results are distinct from the all-POVM theorem.
One-copy variance is not an exact optimal high-confidence sample complexity;
the concentration conversion supplied here is sufficient. No strongest-method
end-to-end advantage or final novelty clearance is established.
